questions.prompt: What does volatile guarantee for a single field?

options.text: Visibility and ordering for that field's reads/writes
That GC will never collect the object

questions.explanation: volatile provides visibility and happens-before for that field. Compound updates still need atomics or locks.

questions.prompt: When are virtual threads a good default?

options.text: Replacing all locks with busy-spin loops

questions.explanation: Virtual threads shine on I/O-bound imperative code. CPU-bound work still needs careful pooling; they don't remove the need for correct synchronization.

questions.prompt: What does this print (assuming no reordering surprises — think happens-before via join)?
questions.explanation: Thread.join() establishes happens-before with the joined thread's termination, so the write to x is visible.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: Spring enables virtual threads with spring.threads.virtual._____=true
questions.explanation: Property is spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true.

questions.prompt: Write a method that counts distinct words in a sentence (split on whitespace), case-insensitive. Return the count as an int. Print it for "Hello hello WORLD".
questions.explanation: hello/Hello collapse case-insensitively; WORLD is distinct → 2.

questions.prompt: What does the javac compiler produce from a .java source file?

options.text: Native machine code directly executable by the OS

questions.explanation: javac compiles Java source into JVM bytecode (.class files); the JVM then interprets/JIT-compiles it.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct signature for a Java application's main entry point?
questions.explanation: The JVM looks for exactly `public static void main(String[] args)` to start an application.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: System.out.println prints the string followed by a newline.

questions.prompt: Write a program that prints exactly: Hello, JVM!
questions.explanation: System.out.println writes the literal text plus a trailing newline.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of Java's eight primitive types?
questions.explanation: String is a reference type (an object), not one of the 8 primitives (byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, boolean).

questions.prompt: Which statements about `var` are true?

options.text: var infers the type from the initializer
var can be used for instance fields

questions.explanation: var only works for local variables with an initializer; it is resolved at compile time, so Java remains statically typed.

questions.prompt: Unboxing a null wrapper (e.g. Integer to int) throws a _____.
questions.template: unboxing a null Integer throws a _____
questions.explanation: Autoboxing/unboxing calls .intValue() etc. under the hood; calling it on null throws NPE.

questions.prompt: Using var, declare a=7 and b=5 (both int), then print their sum.
questions.explanation: var infers int from the literal initializers; a + b is standard int addition.

questions.prompt: Which operators short-circuit evaluation in Java?
questions.explanation: && and || skip evaluating the right operand when the result is already determined; & and | always evaluate both sides.

questions.prompt: Which Java version introduced switch expressions with arrow labels (JEP 361)?
questions.explanation: Switch expressions became a standard feature in Java 14.

questions.prompt: Which are valid loop constructs in Java?
questions.explanation: Java has for, enhanced for-each, while, and do/while. There is no `until` loop.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: day matches the 6,7 case label of the switch expression, producing "weekend".

questions.prompt: Why should StringBuilder be used inside a loop that builds up text?

options.text: String is immutable, so repeated concatenation creates many intermediate objects
String does not support the + operator

questions.explanation: Each String concatenation in Java creates a new String object; StringBuilder mutates an internal buffer instead.

questions.prompt: Use s1._____(s2) for a case-insensitive String comparison.
questions.explanation: equalsIgnoreCase() compares String content while ignoring case.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: String.formatted substitutes %s with the argument, like String.format.

questions.prompt: Write join(String[] words) using StringBuilder that returns the words separated by a single space with no trailing space. Print join(new String[]{"a","b","c"}).
questions.explanation: Appending a separator only before non-first elements avoids a trailing space.

questions.prompt: What exception is thrown when accessing an array index outside its valid range?
questions.explanation: Arrays throw the more specific ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException for invalid indices.

questions.prompt: Which utility class provides sort, fill, copyOf, equals, and toString for arrays?
questions.explanation: java.util.Arrays holds these static helper methods.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Java arrays are true?

options.text: Length is fixed at creation time
2D arrays are arrays-of-arrays and rows can be jagged

questions.explanation: Java arrays cannot resize; a and b and d are correct.

questions.prompt: Use Arrays._____(nums) for a readable String of an array's contents instead of printing it directly.
questions.explanation: Printing an array directly shows its hash-based identity string; Arrays.toString formats the elements.

questions.prompt: When is method overloading resolved in Java?

options.text: At compile time, based on argument types
At runtime, based on the actual object type

questions.explanation: Overload resolution is a compile-time decision based on the static types of the arguments.

questions.prompt: Which rule applies to varargs parameters?

options.text: A method can declare multiple varargs parameters
The varargs parameter must be the last parameter
Varargs cannot be combined with other parameters
Varargs creates a List, not an array

questions.explanation: Only one varargs parameter is allowed, and it must be the last one in the parameter list.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: The varargs call packs 1,2,3 into an int[], and sum totals them.

questions.prompt: Write two overloaded methods named describe: one for int returning "int:VALUE" and one for String returning "str:VALUE". Print describe(5) then describe("hi") on separate lines.
questions.explanation: Overload resolution picks the int or String version based on the compile-time argument type.

questions.prompt: What does calling this(...) inside a constructor do?

options.text: Calls another constructor of the same class

questions.explanation: this(...) chains to another constructor overload in the same class; super(...) calls the parent constructor.

questions.prompt: Which are benefits of encapsulation (private fields with public methods)?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation controls access and hides internals, but it does not by itself make code thread-safe.

questions.prompt: A subclass constructor calls its parent's constructor with _____(...).
questions.explanation: super(...) invokes the immediate superclass constructor.

questions.prompt: Given an Account class with a constructor(opening balance in cents), deposit(long cents), and balance(): create an Account with opening balance 1000, deposit 250, then print the balance.
questions.explanation: deposit adds cents to the private balanceCents field; 1000 + 250 = 1250.

questions.prompt: What does `final` prevent when applied to a class?
questions.explanation: A final class cannot be extended (subclassed).

questions.prompt: Every Java class ultimately extends which class?
questions.explanation: java.lang.Object is the implicit root of every class hierarchy.

questions.prompt: Which statements about polymorphism and dynamic dispatch are true?

options.text: The overriding method actually invoked is chosen at runtime
A parent-typed variable can reference a subclass instance
abstract classes can be instantiated directly
Composition is often preferable when the relationship isn't a true "is-a"

questions.explanation: abstract classes cannot be instantiated directly; the other statements are correct.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: Even though `a` is declared as Animal, dynamic dispatch calls Dog's overridden speak() at runtime.

questions.prompt: What is a functional interface?

options.text: An interface with exactly one abstract method
Any interface that has default methods
An interface with only static methods
An abstract class with one method

questions.explanation: A functional interface has a single abstract method (SAM), which lets it be implemented with a lambda.

questions.prompt: The annotation that documents a functional interface's intent (and lets the compiler verify it) is @_____.
questions.explanation: @FunctionalInterface causes a compile error if the interface doesn't have exactly one abstract method.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: The lambda implements Greeter's single abstract method, concatenating "Hi " with the argument.

questions.prompt: Create interface Shape with a default method describe() returning "a shape" and an abstract method area() returning double. Implement class Square(side) where area() = side*side. Print new Square(4).describe() then new Square(4).area().
questions.explanation: describe() is inherited from the interface default; area() returns 4*4=16.0 as a double.

questions.prompt: What does the `record` keyword automatically generate?

options.text: Constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode, and toString

questions.explanation: record is a concise immutable data carrier: the compiler generates all of these for you.

questions.prompt: Which Java version introduced sealed classes/interfaces (JEP 409)?
questions.explanation: Sealed classes/interfaces became a standard feature in Java 17.

questions.prompt: Which statements about enums in Java are true?

options.text: They are type-safe sets of constants
They can carry fields and methods
They can be extended by other classes via `extends`
They can be used as switch labels

questions.explanation: Enums implicitly extend java.lang.Enum and cannot be subclassed further by other classes.

questions.prompt: record User(String name, Role role) generates an accessor for the name field called u._____() (not getName()).
questions.explanation: Record accessors are named after the component, not with a get- prefix.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a checked exception?
questions.explanation: IOException must be declared or caught; the others are unchecked RuntimeException subclasses.

questions.prompt: In a try/catch/finally, which block is guaranteed to run regardless of whether an exception occurs?

options.text: Nothing runs if an exception is thrown

questions.explanation: finally always executes (except for JVM exit/crash), typically used for cleanup.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.answer: caught: Index 5 out of bounds for length 2
questions.explanation: Accessing index 5 of a length-2 array throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException with that message, caught and printed.

questions.prompt: Create class Resource implementing AutoCloseable that prints "open" in its constructor and "close" in close(). Use try-with-resources to create one and print "use" inside the block.
questions.explanation: try-with-resources calls close() automatically at the end of the block, even without an exception.

questions.prompt: Which Map implementation keeps its keys in sorted order?
questions.explanation: TreeMap maintains keys in sorted order (via Comparable or a Comparator).

questions.prompt: Which are true about List.of(), Set.of(), and Map.of()?

options.text: You must copy into a mutable collection to modify the result
They are convenience factory methods in java.util

questions.explanation: These factory methods reject null elements and produce immutable collections.

questions.prompt: counts.merge(word, 1, Integer::_____) increments a counter for word, defaulting to 1 if absent.
questions.explanation: Map.merge combines the existing value and 1 using Integer::sum when the key is already present.

questions.prompt: Count occurrences of each word in a String[] using a HashMap<String,Integer> and merge, then print the count for "cat" given words = {"cat","dog","cat"}.
questions.explanation: "cat" appears twice in the array, so merge accumulates its count to 2.

questions.prompt: What is type erasure in Java generics?

options.text: Generic type information is removed at runtime, replaced with raw types and casts
Generics are erased at compile time causing a compile error

questions.explanation: The compiler inserts casts and removes generic type parameters, so `new T[]` and `instanceof List<String>` aren't allowed.

questions.prompt: What does PECS stand for when choosing bounded wildcards?
questions.explanation: Use `? extends T` when reading (producing) and `? super T` when writing (consuming).

questions.prompt: Which are direct consequences of type erasure?

options.text: Generic type parameters are available via reflection at runtime
Raw types exist for backward compatibility

questions.explanation: Type parameters are erased, so reflection sees raw types, not the original generic parameters.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: The bounded generic max method scans the list and returns the largest element, 9.

questions.prompt: Which package holds standard functional interfaces like Function, Predicate, and Supplier?
questions.explanation: java.util.function defines the standard functional interface types used across the Streams API.

questions.prompt: list.forEach(System.out::_____) prints each element on its own line.
questions.explanation: A method reference to println is used as the Consumer<T> for forEach.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: nonBlank.negate() is true for blank strings, so removeIf deletes "" and " ", leaving [hi, ok].

questions.prompt: Declare a Function<Integer,Integer> named square using a lambda that returns its input squared. Print square.apply(5).
questions.explanation: The lambda x -> x * x implements Function<Integer,Integer>.apply, giving 5*5=25.

questions.prompt: Intermediate stream operations like map/filter are:

options.text: Lazy — they don't execute until a terminal operation runs
Executed once eagerly then cached forever
Automatically run on a background thread

questions.explanation: Nothing happens in a stream pipeline until a terminal operation (e.g. collect, forEach) triggers it.

questions.prompt: Which method, added in Java 16, converts a stream directly into an (unmodifiable) List?
questions.explanation: Stream.toList() is shorthand for .collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableList()).

questions.prompt: Which Collectors are standard in java.util.stream.Collectors?
questions.explanation: toList, groupingBy, and partitioningBy are all real Collectors; sortInPlace doesn't exist.

questions.prompt: A stream pipeline can only be traversed _____; reusing it throws IllegalStateException.
questions.explanation: Streams are single-use: once a terminal operation consumes the stream, it cannot be reused.

questions.prompt: What is Optional<T> primarily intended for?

options.text: Replacing all null checks everywhere, including fields
Method parameters that might be missing

questions.explanation: Optional is designed for return types signaling "maybe a value", not for fields or parameters.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an Optional anti-pattern?

options.text: Using Optional as a field type or method parameter
Using orElseThrow for a missing value

questions.explanation: Optional is meant for return types; using it for fields or parameters is discouraged.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: map transforms the present value with toUpperCase; orElse's fallback is unused since a value is present.

questions.prompt: Write findFirstEven(int[] xs) returning Optional<Integer> of the first even number, or Optional.empty(). Print findFirstEven(new int[]{1,3,4,5}).orElse(-1).
questions.explanation: 4 is the first even number in {1,3,4,5}, so Optional.of(4) is returned and orElse(-1) is not used.

questions.prompt: What must be true if two objects are equal according to equals()?

options.text: They must return the same hashCode()
They must be the same object reference

questions.explanation: The equals/hashCode contract requires equal objects to produce the same hash code.

questions.prompt: Which are correct practices when overriding equals/hashCode?

options.text: Use the same set of fields in both
Freely use mutable fields as HashMap keys
Consider using record for immutable value objects

questions.explanation: Mutating a key's fields after insertion breaks HashMap lookups; avoid mutable keys.

questions.prompt: Objects._____(x, y) is a convenient way to compute a hashCode from multiple fields.
questions.explanation: java.util.Objects.hash(...) combines the hashCodes of its arguments.

questions.prompt: Implement equals() and hashCode() for class Point(int x, int y) so two Points with equal coordinates are equal. Print new Point(1,2).equals(new Point(1,2)).
questions.explanation: equals compares x and y field-by-field, both of which match, so the result is true.

questions.prompt: Which class represents a modern filesystem path in java.nio.file?
questions.explanation: java.nio.file.Path (used with java.nio.file.Files) is the modern replacement for java.io.File.

questions.prompt: What is recommended for reading or writing large amounts of data?

options.text: Reading one byte at a time with a raw FileInputStream
Always loading the whole file with Scanner

questions.explanation: Buffering (or NIO channels) reduces the number of costly I/O syscalls compared to unbuffered byte-by-byte access.

questions.prompt: Which are true about java.nio.file usage?

options.text: Files.readString reads an entire file into a String
You should specify StandardCharsets.UTF_8 explicitly rather than relying on the platform default
Files.lines returns a Stream that should be closed
File I/O methods never throw checked exceptions

questions.explanation: Files.readString/writeString/lines can throw IOException, a checked exception.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name() returns the canonical charset name "UTF-8".

questions.prompt: Which JUnit 5 annotation runs the same test logic over multiple sets of inputs?
questions.explanation: @ParameterizedTest combined with @ValueSource/@CsvSource runs one test method across many inputs.

questions.prompt: JUnit 5 setup code that runs before each test method goes in a method annotated @_____.
questions.explanation: @BeforeEach marks per-test setup; @AfterEach marks per-test teardown.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: add(2, 3) evaluates to 5, and 5 == 5 is true.

questions.prompt: Implement static int add(int a, int b) in class Calc. In main, print "PASS" if add(2,3)==5 and add(0,0)==0, otherwise print "FAIL".
questions.explanation: Both assertions hold once add correctly returns a + b, so the program prints PASS.

questions.prompt: Which build tool uses a declarative XML file called pom.xml?
questions.explanation: Maven's project model and dependencies are declared in pom.xml.

questions.prompt: What enforces strong encapsulation between Java modules?
questions.explanation: The JPMS, configured via module-info.java, controls what a module exports and requires.

questions.prompt: Which are true about Maven/Gradle dependency management?

options.text: Both resolve transitive dependencies from repositories
A BOM helps align versions across a family of libraries
Version conflicts can be inspected with dependency-tree tooling
Pinning dependency versions is generally discouraged

questions.explanation: Pinning versions is actually recommended for reproducible builds.

questions.prompt: In a Maven dependency for a test-only library like JUnit, the _____ element is set to "test".
questions.explanation: <scope>test</scope> restricts a dependency to the test classpath only.

questions.prompt: At what default load factor does HashMap resize (double its table and rehash)?
questions.explanation: HashMap's default load factor is 0.75, balancing memory use and lookup speed.

questions.prompt: What happens to a HashMap bucket once it exceeds the treeify threshold (8 entries)?

options.text: It converts to a red-black tree for O(log n) lookup

questions.explanation: Past the treeify threshold, a bucket's linked list becomes a red-black tree to bound worst-case lookup cost.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: Putting the same key twice overwrites the value rather than adding an entry: size stays 1, value becomes 2.

questions.prompt: Create a HashMap<String,Integer> pre-sized for 16 entries. Put keys "a","b","a" using merge(key,1,Integer::sum), then print the final count for key "a".
questions.explanation: "a" appears twice, so merge accumulates its count to 2 regardless of the initial pre-sizing.

questions.prompt: What should you generally use instead of managing raw Threads directly?
questions.explanation: ExecutorService manages a pool of reusable threads and lets you submit tasks without manual thread lifecycle handling.

questions.prompt: Which provide thread-safe coordination for shared mutable state?

options.text: A plain HashMap with no locking

questions.explanation: A plain HashMap is not thread-safe and needs external synchronization or a concurrent alternative.

questions.prompt: AtomicInteger provides lock-free read-modify-write using _____ (compare-and-swap).
questions.explanation: Atomic classes use CAS instructions to update values without traditional locking.

questions.prompt: Using an ExecutorService with a single thread, submit a task that returns 21*2, then print the Future's result.
questions.explanation: The submitted Callable computes 21*2=42, and Future.get() blocks until that result is available.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does `volatile` NOT guarantee?

options.text: Atomicity for compound updates like i++
Visibility of writes to other threads
Ordering relative to other volatile accesses
That the JIT won't reorder across the volatile access

questions.explanation: volatile guarantees visibility and ordering for that field, but not atomicity for read-modify-write like i++.

questions.prompt: Which action establishes happens-before with a subsequent lock of the same monitor?
questions.explanation: The JMM guarantees unlock of a monitor happens-before a subsequent lock of that same monitor.

questions.prompt: Which are appropriate uses of a `volatile` field?

options.text: A boolean shutdown/running flag checked by multiple threads
Publishing an immutable reference after construction
Implementing a thread-safe counter with counter++
Coordinating a read-modify-write operation with no other synchronization

questions.explanation: Compound operations like counter++ are not atomic even on a volatile field; use AtomicInteger instead.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: Two calls to incrementAndGet() atomically bump the counter from 0 to 2.

questions.prompt: Which JEP introduced virtual threads?
questions.explanation: JEP 444 finalized virtual threads in Java 21.

questions.prompt: Executors._____() creates an executor that runs each submitted task on its own virtual thread.
questions.explanation: This factory method creates a virtual-thread-per-task ExecutorService.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: The submitted task runs on a virtual thread and returns "done", which get() retrieves.

questions.prompt: Using Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor(), submit a task that computes the sum of integers 1..100 and print the result via Future.get().
questions.explanation: The sum of integers from 1 to 100 is 5050 (n*(n+1)/2 for n=100).

questions.prompt: Why is constructor injection generally preferred in Spring?

options.text: Dependencies are explicit and fields can be made final
It avoids needing any dependency configuration at all
It is the only injection style modern Spring supports
It disables the Spring application context

questions.explanation: Constructor injection makes required dependencies explicit and lets you mark fields final, which keeps tests honest.

questions.prompt: Why does calling another @Transactional method on `this` from within the same class often silently skip the transaction?

options.text: The call bypasses the Spring AOP proxy
Self-invocation is blocked by the JVM
Transactions cannot be nested in Spring

questions.explanation: Spring's declarative transactions are implemented via a proxy; calling through `this` skips that proxy entirely.

questions.prompt: Which statements about HikariCP pool sizing are true?

options.text: Size the pool for real concurrent DB users, not the number of threads
Virtual threads can increase the number of requests waiting on the pool
REQUIRES_NEW propagation can open an additional database connection
Read-only transactions never hold a connection

questions.explanation: Read-only transactions still hold a connection for the duration of the method.

questions.prompt: The annotation @_____ marks a class as a Spring-managed service bean (as used on OrderService).
questions.explanation: @Service is a specialization of @Component used for service-layer beans.

questions.prompt: Which garbage collector is the default, balanced collector in modern JVMs?
questions.explanation: G1 (Garbage-First) is the default collector, balancing throughput and pause times for most applications.

questions.prompt: Which collectors target sub-millisecond pause times for large heaps?
questions.explanation: ZGC and Shenandoah are designed for very low pause times even with large heaps, trading some throughput.

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: Five short-lived Object instances are created (illustrating the generational hypothesis); count ends at 5.

questions.prompt: Write containerFlags(int mb) that returns "-Xms{mb}m -Xmx{mb}m" using the same value for min and max heap (a container best practice). Print containerFlags(512).
questions.explanation: Setting -Xms equal to -Xmx avoids heap resize churn inside a fixed-memory container.
